text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD

- The 1998 and 1999 budgets will have much bigger gaps than Finance Minister Rudolf Edlinger admitted. Unless major counter measures are taken the budget will fall short by 30 to 40 billion schillings next year and 80 to 90 billion in 1999 due to cost increases.

- The conservative People's Party has officially voiced its full support of Austrian entry to NATO. Defence Minister Werner Fasslabend says joining the military alliance would not cost the defence ministry any more than it spends presently.

- The opposition Greens want President Thomas Klestil to clarify his role in the handling of the 1989 Kurdish affair, in which the Iranian suspected killers of three Kurdish activists in Vienna were released.
- Austrians celebrated the designation of the historic Schoenbrunn Palace, former summer residence of the imperial family, as a World Heritage Site by UNESCO.

Hans Sallmutter, head of the union of privately employed has sharply criticised a decision by Vienna city council to withdraw from AVZ, Anteilsverwaltung Zentralsparkasse, which he says will be counter-productive for the whole savings bank sector.
DIE PRESSE
- Austrian mountaineer and Tibetan explorer Heinrich Harrer admitted he was a member of the Nazi party and Hitler's elite SS.
- Deputy head of die Erste savings bank Wolfgang Ulrich says the savings banks should not fall victim to cost cutting in order to fulfil the Maastricht criteria.
- Exports are driving a hesitant economic recovery in the early part of the year, according to a recent survey by the chamber of economy. Domestic demand remains slack.
- The postal savings bank will have a new board of directors from August 1. A cooperation agreement with the postal service is still up in the air.
- The regional hypo banks refuse full privatisation. The banks are against a total pullout by the provinces from the sector.
- A decision on a road pricing system for trucks should be made by September.
KURIER
- Conservative education minister Elisabeth Gehrer saays more teachers are needed to cope with the increase of 5000 students at secondary school level.
- Energy prices in Austria are about average in Europe, according to the European Statistical office Eurostat.
- The European Union is considering taxing wine producers who are currently exempt from drinks taxes.
WIRTSCHAFTSBLATT
- Cooperation between the postal service and postal savings bank is faltering over an agreement on financial products and rent for postal counters.
